Diabetes mellitus may have a neutral or slightly reduced impact on the efficacy of FDG-PET (Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography) scans for diagnosing cervical cancer. While the original study mentioned in one of the retrieved matches suggests that the accuracy of PET scans is not significantly affected by diabetes, it does not provide information on whether diabetes itself has an impact on the diagnostic performance.

However, based on another study mentioned in a different match, patients with mild to moderate diabetes mellitus who underwent FDG-PET scans for cervical cancer reported no significant differences in disease-free survival compared to those without diabetes. This suggests that while diabetes may have some influence on the accuracy of PET scans, it does not significantly impact their utility in diagnosing cervical cancer.

It is essential to note that this is a general conclusion based on available data and should be interpreted with caution. More research is needed to fully understand the relationship between diabetes mellitus and the diagnostic performance of FDG-PET scans for cervical cancer.

In summary, while diabetes may have some influence on the accuracy of FDG-PET scans, its impact on their efficacy in diagnosing cervical cancer appears to be neutral or slightly reduced, and more research is needed to fully understand this relationship.
